title: Canonical coefficient-duality maps on a small ringed site
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site, small in the chosen module universe [def-weil-size-convention], where $\mathcal O$ is a sheaf of commutative rings. Use its category of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], the unbounded derived category $D(\mathcal O)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the derived tensor obtained from the total tensor complex after K-flat resolutions [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves, def-pc-kflat-complex, lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], and $H(A,B)=R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(A,B)$ obtained from K-injective resolutions [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Regard $\mathcal O$ as a complex concentrated in degree zero and write $A^\vee=H(A,\mathcal O)$. For arbitrary $A,B\in D(\mathcal O)$ there are canonical morphisms
$$e_{A,B}:B\otimes_{\mathcal O}^{\mathbf L}A^\vee\longrightarrow H(A,B),\qquad b_A:A\longrightarrow H(A^\vee,\mathcal O).$$
The first is natural contravariantly in $A$ and covariantly in $B$; the second is natural covariantly in $A$. The map $e_{A,B}$ is the derived internal-composition map $H(\mathcal O,B)\otimes^{\mathbf L}H(A,\mathcal O)\to H(A,B)$ after the canonical identification $B\cong H(\mathcal O,B)$. The map $b_A$ is the transpose of coefficient evaluation with its tensor factors exchanged by the Koszul symmetry. Both maps are normalized on ordinary representatives as follows. Let $E,F$ be complexes of $\mathcal O$-modules representing $A,B$, with $F$ K-flat, put $D=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,\mathcal O[0])$, and suppose that $D$ is K-flat and that the maps $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,\mathcal O[0])\to\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,\mathcal I^\bullet(\mathcal O[0]))$ and $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,F)\to\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,\mathcal I^\bullet(F))$ induced by the fixed K-injective resolutions of [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] are quasi-isomorphisms, so that $D$ represents $A^\vee$ and $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,F)$ represents $H(A,B)$. Then, under these identifications and the comparison $Q\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes D)\cong B\otimes^{\mathbf L}A^\vee$ of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], $e_{A,B}$ is the image of the chain map $\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes D)\to\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,F)$ sending $y\otimes\phi\in F^p\otimes D^q$ to the degree-$(p+q)$ map $x\mapsto y\,\phi(x)$, with no sign. Similarly, for any complex $E$ representing $A$ such that, with $D=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,\mathcal O[0])$, the maps $D\to\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,\mathcal I^\bullet(\mathcal O[0]))$ and $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(D,\mathcal O[0])\to\mathcal Hom^\bullet(D,\mathcal I^\bullet(\mathcal O[0]))$ are quasi-isomorphisms (no flatness required), $b_A$ is, under these identifications, the image of the chain map $E\to\mathcal Hom^\bullet(D,\mathcal O[0])$, $x\mapsto\bigl(\phi\mapsto(-1)^{|x||\phi|}\phi(x)\bigr)$ for homogeneous $x,\phi$. Hom complexes carry the differential $d(f)=d_{\mathrm{target}}f-(-1)^{\deg f}f d_{\mathrm{source}}$ [def-pur-hom-complex] and total tensor complexes the differential of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. For every object $U$ of $\mathcal C$, restriction to the localized ringed site $(\mathcal C/U,\mathcal O_U)$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] takes both maps to the corresponding canonical maps on that site, under the canonical restriction comparisons for derived tensor [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] and derived internal Hom [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction]; slice restriction is the exact module pullback of [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. No perfectness, boundedness or invertibility of either displayed map is asserted.

proof.text:
Let $\epsilon_{K,M}:H(K,M)\otimes^{\mathbf L}K\to M$ be the image of $1_{H(K,M)}$ under the adjunction of step 1. For $K,L,M$ define $c_{K,L,M}$ by transposing the composite
$$(H(L,M)\otimes^{\mathbf L}H(K,L))\otimes^{\mathbf L}K\to H(L,M)\otimes^{\mathbf L}L\to M,$$
where the first arrow is $1\otimes\epsilon_{K,L}$ after rebracketing, and the second is $\epsilon_{L,M}$. Thus $c:H(L,M)\otimes^{\mathbf L}H(K,L)\to H(K,M)$. On Hom-complex representatives it is $(f,g)\mapsto f\circ g$: uncurrying either construction sends $(f,g,x)$ to $f(g(x))$. The identity $d(fg)=(df)g+(-1)^{|f|}f(dg)$ from [def-pur-hom-complex] verifies that this is the total chain-composition map used by Stacks 0A98. Its derived independence follows from step 1. It is natural in $K,M$ and dinatural in the middle object $L$: for $u:L\to L'$, $f(ug)=(fu)g$ expresses the two maps from $H(L',M)\otimes^{\mathbf L}H(K,L)$ to $H(K,M)$.

The unit-Hom isomorphism [lem-sc-hom-complex-unit-iso] applied to the K-injective target identifies $H(\mathcal O,B)$ with $B$. Set $e_{A,B}=c_{A,\mathcal O,B}$ under this identification. Its transpose under step 1 is
$$B\otimes^{\mathbf L}A^\vee\otimes^{\mathbf L}A\xrightarrow{1\otimes\epsilon_{A,\mathcal O}}B\otimes^{\mathbf L}\mathcal O\cong B.$$
For $u:A'\to A$ and $v:B\to B'$, naturality of this composite gives $H(u,v)e_{A,B}=e_{A',B'}(v\otimes H(u,1_{\mathcal O}))$. Define $b_A$ by transposing $A\otimes^{\mathbf L}A^\vee\xrightarrow{\tau}A^\vee\otimes^{\mathbf L}A\xrightarrow{\epsilon_{A,\mathcal O}}\mathcal O$, using step 1 with $K=A^\vee$. Both sides of $H(H(u,1),1)b_{A'}=b_Au$ transpose to evaluation on $(u(x'),\phi)$, proving covariance. These constructions use the dual of $A$, not evaluation of $A^\vee$ against its own dual.

proof.text: For the first normalization choose a K-flat resolution $r:P\to E$. The assumed map $D\to\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,I(\mathcal O))$ identifies $D$ with $A^\vee$; precomposition with $r$ is a quasi-isomorphism by [lem-pur-rhom-well-defined]. By the componentwise adjunction in step 1, the pairing $D\otimes P\to\mathcal O[0]$, $(\phi,x)\mapsto\phi(r(x))$, followed by $\mathcal O[0]\to I(\mathcal O)$, is $\epsilon_{A,\mathcal O}$ on these models. The quasi-isomorphism $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,F)\to\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,I(F))$, followed by precomposition with $r$, identifies the stated target with $H(A,B)$. The transpose in step 4 sends $(y,\phi,x)$ to $y\phi(r(x))$, followed by $F\to I(F)$. Currying gives precisely precomposition with $r$ of $x\mapsto y\phi(x)$, followed by $F\to I(F)$; hence that chain map represents $e_{A,B}$. The tensor comparisons apply by step 2. For $|y|=p,|\phi|=q$, [def-pur-hom-complex] gives $d_D\phi=-(-1)^q\phi d_E$; thus the tensor differential gives $d_Fy\,\phi+(-1)^{p+q+1}y\phi d_E$, equal to the Hom differential of $x\mapsto y\phi(x)$. No sign is inserted in the map itself.

source.place: Tag 08JD; Tag 0A98; Hom differential in Section 0A8X

proof.text: For the second normalization put $D=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,\mathcal O[0])$ and choose K-flat resolutions $P\to E$ and $T\to D$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. The first assumed quasi-isomorphism identifies $D$ with $A^\vee$. On $T\otimes P$, evaluation is $(t,x)\mapsto t(x)$, where the resolution maps into $D,E$ are understood, followed by $\mathcal O\to I(\mathcal O)$; this follows by uncurrying in step 1. After the exchange in step 2, the transpose is $x\mapsto(\phi\mapsto(-1)^{|x||\phi|}\phi(x))$. Postcomposing this ordinary chain map by $\mathcal O\to I(\mathcal O)$ and precomposing the Hom variable by $T\to D$ gives exactly that transpose on $P,T$. The second assumed quasi-isomorphism and [lem-pur-rhom-well-defined] identify its target with $H(A^\vee,\mathcal O)$, so the ordinary map represents $b_A$. For $|x|=a,|\phi|=-a-1$, the outer Hom differential evaluated at $\phi$ is $-(-1)^a b(x)(d_D\phi)$. Here $d_D\phi=(-1)^a\phi d_E$ and $b(x)$ on degree $-a$ has sign $(-1)^a$. The product sign is therefore $(-1)^{a+1}$, equal to $b(d_Ex)(\phi)$ since $(a+1)(-a-1)\equiv a+1$ modulo $2$. Other degree components vanish. The ordinary signed bidual chain map and its uniqueness are now proved directly in Lean: form the sheaf bidual x maps to evaluation at x, compose with each actual Hom-product projection and multiply the (i,q) component by (-1)^(iq). The product universal property gives the degree map. Project the two chain-map composites, use the Hom differential with zero differential on the coefficient unit, and evaluate at a local dual section. Naturality of the differential and the identity -(-1)^i (-1)^(i(q+1)) (-(-1)^q) = (-1)^((i+1)q) prove equality. For uniqueness, use product extensionality: the degree-zero coefficient component is determined by RingedSiteBidualFormula, and every other coefficient degree is a zero object. The derived-normalization argument in the preceding sentences remains the plan for the remaining normalization theorem.

source.place: Tag 0A97, coefficient-unit specialization; Section 0A8X, signed bidual chain map

proof.text: For $U\in\mathcal C$, use the localized coefficients of [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Restriction is exact by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], sends K-injectives to K-injectives by [lem-pur-kinjective-restrict-localized], and compares derived tensor and Hom by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] and [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction]. The tensor-pullback node applies with $u=j_U$: localization is a morphism of topoi $j_U^{-1}\dashv j_{U*}$ with $j_U^{-1}$ exact (Stacks Section 00XZ), and $j_U^{-1}\mathcal O=\mathcal O_U$, so $u^*$ is restriction and restricted K-flat flat-term complexes stay K-flat with flat terms. Compute steps 1--4 with K-flat, flat-term representatives and K-injective targets: their restrictions are such representatives on the slice, and the Hom and tensor comparisons are the sectionwise identifications on them. On each object $V\to U$ the uncurrying map still sends $(f,x)$ to $f(x)$, composition sends $(f,g,x)$ to $f(g(x))$, and exchange multiplies by the same $(-1)^{|x||\phi|}$. Thus these comparisons preserve the adjunct identity that defines $\epsilon$, the composite defining $c$, and the transpose defining $b$. Adjunction is a bijection, so the compared maps are exactly $e$ and $b$ on the slice. This argument uses arbitrary resolution models, not the extra hypotheses of the optional ordinary normalizations.
